english: Let $S$ be the set of all real numbers $x>0$, $x\neq\dfrac12$, $x\neq2$, satisfying
Then the sum of all the elements of $S$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $S$ उन सभी वास्तविक संख्याओं $x>0$, $x\neq\dfrac12$, $x\neq2$ का समुच्चय है जो
को संतुष्ट करती हैं। तब $S$ के सभी अवयवों का योग ______ है।
solution_full: The bases $2x$ and $\dfrac x2$ are positive and different from $1$ for $x>0,\ x\neq\dfrac12,\ x\neq2$; the arguments $16x$ and $\dfrac{x}{16}$ are positive.
Change of base to base $2$: $\log_{2x}(16x)=\dfrac{\log_2 16+\log_2x}{\log_22+\log_2x}=\dfrac{t+4}{t+1}$ and $\log_{x/2}\dfrac{x}{16}=\dfrac{t-4}{t-1}$.
(The left side is unchanged when $t$ is replaced by $-t$, i.e. $x$ by $\dfrac1x$, so the roots come as a reciprocal pair.)
So $S=\left\{4,\dfrac14\right\}$ and the sum of its elements is $4.25$.
originality_note: New: a product of two variable-base logarithms with bases 2x and x/2 and arguments 16x and x/16 that is invariant under x -> 1/x, so the roots form a reciprocal pair (way 4). Closest known: log_x 2 . log_{2x} 2 = log_{4x} 2 and similar base-substitution equations. Different because: the symmetry t -> -t makes the equation a pure t^2 equation and the answer a sum of reciprocals.

concept_use.Logarithmic equations with a variable ba: Both factors have variable bases (2x and x/2); with t = log_2 x the equation becomes t^2 = 4 and both roots are checked against the base conditions.

stem_review: Read as a student: every function has a stated domain, every symbol is introduced before use, every condition is given, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed with sympy/mpmath and is unique and equal to the Answer Plan; no hyperbolic functions or asymptotes. Checked: mpmath root search on (0,1/2), (1/2,2), (2,100) finds only 0.25 and 4; the answer 4.25 is a positive decimal as planned. Changed: No change.
key_step: Converting both variable-base logs to t = log_2 x and solving the resulting quadratic.
justification: Routine chain: change of base, a quadratic in t and a base check; no real insight. Same kind as 2024-P1-Q8 (L2), the official logarithm equation question.
